correctness.rationale: For real unit vectors, differentiating the smooth fourth-power norm gives orthogonality x1^3 y1+x2^3 y2=0. Signed coordinate symmetries give x=(a,b) with a,b>=0 and a^4+b^4=1; every unit orthogonal direction is plus or minus (b^3,-a^3)/(a^12+b^12)^(1/4). The quartic expansion eliminates the linear term and gives 1+lambda^4+6A lambda^2+4B lambda^3. With u=a^2 b^2, A=u/sqrt(1-3u^2) ranges continuously over [0,1] and B^2=A(1-A^2); choose B negative. The normalized denominator F has boundary values at least one and tends to one uniformly in A as lambda tends to infinity; an interior test point is below one, so its global minimum is attained inside. The stationary equations are 3C=lambda(1-3A^2) and 3A(1-lambda^4)=C lambda(3-lambda^4). Substitution first gives lambda^4=1/A^2, then (1-3t)^4-81t^2(1-t)^2=(3t+1)(18t^2-15t+1)=0 for t=A^2. Only t=(5-sqrt(17))/12 has t<1/3. Substitution yields F=(5-sqrt(17))/2 and reciprocal (5+sqrt(17))/4. Uniform boundary control and unique feasible critical point establish the global optimum, not numerical enumeration. Independent 70-digit decimal arithmetic checks the stationary equations to residuals below 1e-68 and value 1.228911696999467; the proof is analytic.
residual_risks: Real two-dimensional exponent-four invariant only; arithmetic checks do not certify unrelated exponents or dimensions.

value.rationale: The generalized rectangular constant is a established geometric invariant, and the same-invariant primary article explicitly identifies the gap between general estimates and exact values. Real ell_4^2 is the first non-Hilbert even-power planar case with a closed algebraic Birkhoff-orthogonality reduction. Its exact value and the coefficient relation B^2=A(1-A^2) form a natural sharp benchmark for general estimates; a researcher studying this invariant can need this exact fact without a general theorem. This is not classical-table recomputation or an arbitrary numerical slice.
residual_risks: No assertion about general mu_p, complex scalars or higher dimensions.
